title.point: We are those who are being strengthened, empowered, by God.

thisWeekSong.title: Be Strong and of Good Courage

lyricsCentered.text:
Be strong and of good courage,
Do not be afraid, neither be dismayed,

For Jehovah your God is with you,
Wherever you go.

lastWeekReview.title: Gideon—The Defeat of Midian
bullets: Israel went back to their old evil ways, so God let the MIDIANITES oppress them for seven years — until they cried out to God.
God chose GIDEON to lead just 300 men against an enemy army as huge as a swarm of locusts.
To strengthen Gideon, God let him overhear a DREAM about a barley loaf toppling the tent — a sign that God had given the victory.
Each of the 300 men carried a TRUMPET and a torch hidden in a pitcher, and did exactly what Gideon did.
When they blew the trumpets and smashed the pitchers, God made the enemy swing their SWORDS at one another — God won the battle!
The people wanted Gideon to rule, but he gave all the CREDIT to God — because God, not Gideon, had won.
lastWeekReview.discussion: This week, did you remember to give GOD the credit when something went well — instead of taking it for yourself? Share how God took care of you!
lastWeekReview.verseQuote: “…I will not rule over you…Jehovah will rule over you.” — Judges 8:23

kidsContent.text: Before Samson was even born, the Angel of Jehovah told his mother she would have a son who was SET APART as a Nazarite — never cutting his hair, absolutely for God from the very start.
As Samson grew, God EMPOWERED him with extraordinary strength. One day a young lion roared and rushed at him — and Samson tore it apart with his bare hands! One man against a lion!

God gave him so much strength that he defeated THIRTY men all by himself. Another time his enemies tied him up with ropes — but the ropes melted away, he grabbed a jawbone, and defeated ONE THOUSAND men!
Samson had faith in God, and God made him a judge who led Israel for TWENTY years.
🌟 Every amazing thing Samson did came from one place — God empowered him and gave him his might!

image.caption: God empowers Samson with extraordinary strength

kidsContent.text: God is still strengthening His people today! Not to fight a thousand men with a jawbone — but to do the RIGHT thing when it feels far too hard for us on our own.

Have you ever needed to speak up? One time when the storyteller was young, some friends began making fun of a serving one who had always cared for them. She wanted to say something kind to stop the teasing — but she was AFRAID the others would laugh at her.
She thought it was too hard… but she asked God, and He gave her the strength to speak up. And the other children agreed! God EMPOWERED her to do the right thing.
🌟 When something right feels too hard, we don’t do it in our own strength — we are empowered, made strong, by God!

lesson.practicePoint: This week, when you know the right thing to do but it feels too hard — like speaking up kindly for a serving one, or doing right when it’s not popular — ask God for His strength. He empowers us, just like He empowered Samson!

memoryVerse.text: Finally, be empowered in the Lord and in the might of His strength.
memoryVerse.application: To “empower” means to make strong. God gave Samson amazing strength to do impossible things. And today God still strengthens US — to do hard, right things, like speaking up for what is right. His might, not ours!

activity.title: 💪 Empowered by God — Strength for the Hard Thing

parts.text: Materials: A soft “jawbone” prop (foam or rolled paper), a length of yarn or crepe-paper “ropes,” and a few index cards with hard-but-right situations written on them.
Setup: Explain that Samson was strong only because GOD empowered him. We can’t be strong on our own either — we ask God, and He strengthens us to do what is right.
Round 1 — Snap the Ropes: Loosely tie a child’s wrists with crepe-paper “ropes.” On “God empowers you!” they break free — just like Samson’s ropes melted away. God gives the strength!

Round 2 — The Hard Thing: A child draws a card (“Friends are teasing a serving one,” “Everyone’s doing something wrong,” “I’m scared to speak up”). Before acting, everyone prays: “God, please empower me!”
Round 3 — Act It Out: The child does the right thing in the situation — speaking up kindly, walking away, telling the truth — showing how God’s strength carried them through.
📖 Connection: Samson’s might came from God, not himself. When the right thing feels too hard, God empowers US to do it!

rolePlayScript.text: Scene: The church hallway after a meeting. A few kids stand in a group, giggling. Maya walks up and hears them making fun of Brother Tim, a serving one who always sets up their class.
Long ago God empowered Samson to tear a lion and defeat a thousand men. Today, God still gives His people strength — sometimes to do a thing that feels just as hard.
Did you see Brother Tim trip on the cord? Ha! He’s so clumsy. Somebody should tell him to watch where he’s going.
(quietly, to herself) That’s not nice… Brother Tim sets up our whole room every week. I should say something. But what if they laugh at ME?
Maya’s heart pounded. Speaking up felt too hard. So she did what God’s people do — she prayed inside.
(whispering) God, this is too hard for me. Please empower me. Give me Your strength to do the right thing.
Maya takes a deep breath and steps into the group.
Hey — Brother Tim carries all our chairs and tables every single week. I don’t think we should make fun of him. He really takes care of us.
(pausing) …Yeah. You’re right. That was kind of mean. He does do a lot for us.
I felt bad laughing too. Let’s go say thank you to him instead.
Maya thought it would be too hard — but God gave her the strength, just like He empowered Samson. The right thing happened, because God made her strong.
I was so scared… but God really did give me the strength when I asked Him!
We are empowered, made strong, by God — to do the right thing even when it’s hard!

description.text: Setup: Split into two teams. At each team’s far end, loosely loop a length of crepe-paper “rope” around a chair or a willing teammate’s wrists.
Rules: One runner at a time races down, shouts “God empowers me!”, snaps the crepe-paper rope, then races back to tag the next runner.
Out: If you snap the rope before shouting the words, you re-tie it and go again — the strength comes from God, so we call on Him first!
Finish: First team to have every runner break free and return wins the round.
📖 Connection: When Samson’s enemies tied him up, God made the ropes melt away. God gives His people strength for what looks impossible!
Materials: Crepe paper or yarn, two chairs, open space
Setup: Set up 3–4 “strength” stations around the room — bear crawls, a beanbag “lion” to carry, a “jawbone” (foam bat) beanbag knock-down, and a wall sit.
Rules: Kids rotate through the stations in small groups. Before each station they say together, “God, make me strong!”
Scoring: This isn’t about who’s strongest — every child who finishes the circuit and calls on God gets a cheer from the whole group.
Twist: At the last station, call out a “hard right thing” (like “tell the truth”) — the group acts strong and does it together.
📖 Connection: Samson’s might was never his own — it was God’s. We ask God for strength for both our bodies and our choices!
Materials: Beanbags, a foam bat, floor markers, open space
Choose a leader to call out “strong-man” moves along an outdoor path — log steps, big rock lifts (pretend), hill climbs, and “push the gate.”
Goal: At each stop, before the strong move, the whole group calls out together, “God, please empower me!” — then does the move.
Rule: Nobody has to be the strongest — we help each other, because our strength comes from God, not from showing off.
Finish: Gather at the end and thank God that He strengthens us — for hard moves AND for doing what is right.
Materials: Just an open outdoor space with a few natural landmarks

outdoor.tip: 💪 The lesson is empowering: Samson’s might came entirely from God, and God still strengthens us today. Help the kids connect physical “strength” to the real point — asking God for might to do the right, hard thing.
